question.text: About 40 members of the Parliament in the UK represent this country, home to the cities of Gwynedd and Swansea.
question.clue: Soldiers from this country often wore leeks in their caps during the middle ages, and the border between this country and its eastern neighbor was ruled by a class of "marcher lords" and marked by Offa's Dyke.

swap.text: The Magna Carta was signed by this king, the youngest of five sons of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine.
swap.clue: He failed to reclaim Normandy from France after his allies lost to Philip Augustus at the battle of Bouvines.

question.leadin: In addition to being a British Prime Minister, this man also wrote novels.
question.text: This man rose to power when his party was divided over the decision to repeal the Corn Laws, and was the only British Prime Minister of Jewish birth.
question.clue: While not in politics, this man authored the novel Sybil, or the Two Nations.

swap.text: At the end of the War of Spanish Secession, Britain gained this overseas possession on the Southern coast of Spain. Its namesake Rock is one of the Pillars of Hercules.
swap.clue: Spain gave up Minorca and this territory following the Treaty of Utrecht, and it is home to a mountain once considered the northern "Pillar of Hercules."

question.leadin: Answer the following about Christmas in British history.
question.text: Celebrating Christmas was banned during the rule of this man, who served as Lord Protector after Charles I was executed at the end of the English Civil War.
question.clue: Under the reign of this ruler, militias attempted to abolish stage plays and Christmas traditions.

swap.leadin: This ruler prefixed the Ten Commandments to his Doom Book.
swap.text: Name this Anglo-Saxon king of Wessex who compelled Guthrum to convert to Christianity.
swap.clue: He personally translated from Latin works such as Bede's Ecclesiastical History and Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy.

question.text: This British wartime Prime Minister came to power after the 1916 fall of Henry Herbert Asquith. He also led the creation of the British welfare state and oversaw the Partition of Ireland in 1920.
question.clue: This man served as the Minister of Munitions and had a seven year stint as the Chancellor of the Exchequer.

swap.leadin: The Heptarchy was a collection of seven kingdoms of these people.
swap.text: Name these people whose kingdoms included states like Wessex and Northumbria. Sutton Hoo is an archaeological burial site of these people who migrated to one region along with the Jutes.
swap.clue: By then they would also divide into two groups, with the western one being founded by Cerdic, though it was Cerdic's grandson Egbert who was the first of them to be recognized as a great king.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Queen Matilda of England.
question.text: This cousin of Matilda usurped the throne on the death of Henry I in 1135. He warred with Matilda and her son Henry II until 1153.
question.clue: Much of his reign was dominated by civil war, and he was unable to secure the throne for his son, Eustace, even after his defeat of a woman whose son managed to acquire Normandy and Aquitaine.

swap.leadin: As this battle of the War of the Roses began, the King's forces positioned themselves on Ambien Hill.
swap.text: Name this battle between Richard III and a Tudor opponent who had fled to Brittany after the Battle of Tewkesbury but now returned with an army of five thousand.
swap.clue: The winner here later had to deal with uprisings led by the supposed Earl of Warwick and Perkin Warbeck.

question.text: This Roman goddess of the hunt was equivalent to the Greek Artemis.
question.clue: A fascist Mitford sister shares this forename with a woman who visited Angola as part of her work with the HALO Trust.

swap.leadin: Some crewmembers of this ship later died in the shipwreck of the Pandora.
swap.text: Name this trading ship whose crew mutinied against captain William Bligh.
swap.clue: John Fryer wrote a narrative that described how nineteen men were cast off in its tiny launch and made an improbable 3,000 mile voyage from Tofoa to Timor.

question.text: This British sociologist criticized the state of 19th-century women's education in the 1837 tract Society in America. She also wrote Illustrations of Political Economy.
question.clue: One of the most famous writers in the world during her lifetime for works such as anti-slavery tract Life in America, who is this writer better known today for her translations of Auguste Comte and early writings on women's rights?

swap.leadin: The eighth British monarch of this name abdicated the throne to marry the American divorcee Wallis Simpson, and was succeeded by his younger brother George VI, who made him Duke of Windsor.
swap.text: Give this name shared by that monarch and Queen Victoria's successor, who was the seventh of this name.
swap.clue: The Hundred Years' War began under one king of this name, and another fought the Second Barons' War against Simon de Montfort.

question.leadin: This person's tenure as Lord Admiral of England saw the creation of the Navy Board as well as the sinking of the Mary Rose.
question.text: Name this second chief regent for Edward VI, after Edward Seymour. This statesman orchestrated the downfall of the Duke of Somerset before replacing William Paulet as Lord President of the Council.
question.answerHtml: J ohn Dudley [accept the 1st Duke of Northumberland , or the Earl of Warwick , or Viscount Lisle ; prompt on Dudley ]

swap.text: You flee to the valley of this river, which was agreed to form the border between Anglo-Saxon and Danish lands. Edward was crowned upon this river at Kingston, part of modern-day London.
swap.clue: That project was a sewer system created after this river's Great Stink.

question.leadin: During this event, the monk Gregory of Huntington purchased a collection of holy texts so that he could translate them, saving them from certain destruction.
question.text: Name this 1290 event where a certain group associated with the death of Saint William of Norwich was told to leave cities such as York and London.
question.answer: expulsion of the Jews from England
question.clue: The Domus Conversorum was eventually converted to a home for clerks after this event.

swap.leadin: This man fell in love with Sophia Hopkey during his tour of America.
swap.text: Identify this co-founder of the Holy Club at Oxford. His brother Charles wrote hymns like "O for a Thousand Tongues to Sing".

question.leadin: Answer the following about European armies' use of spears.
question.text: At the Battle of Bannockburn, the Scottish under Thomas Randolph effectively used a circular variant of this formation.
question.clue: At Falkirk, Wallace made use of this military formation, which consisted of tightly packed spearmen arranged in a circle. The name of this military formation can be translated to modern English as "shield wall."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a reoccurring theme from English economic history. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this general term describing the conversion of common fields and grazing lands into privately owned and operated property, whether or not it involved fencing off the land.
swap.clue: It's not religious, but the terms "leveller" and "digger" were originally applied to opponents of this policy, which gained momentum after an invention by Jethro Tull.
